scope: P7: Stapp rocket-sled stop (topic #1 of GROWTH-PLAN), body at risk, real 1954 opener
script: [tense] This man went from six hundred thirty-two miles an hour to zero in under a second and a half. [curious] Air Force doctor John Stapp did it on purpose. [surprised] The stop hit him with forty-six times his body weight. He survived, and became the fastest man on Earth.

new_claims.claim: 10 Dec 1954, Sonic Wind No. 1, Holloman AFB: reached 632 mph ('six hundred thirty-two miles an hour')
Slowed to a stop in 1.4 s ('under a second and a half'); on-screen stopwatch runs 0.00-1.40 s in real time
Peak 46.2 g during the stop ('forty-six times his body weight'; 46.2 g = force 46.2x body weight)
new_claims.source: Wikipedia; Smithsonian NASM ('approximately four tons (46.2 g)')

new_claims.claim: Air Force doctor (USAF flight surgeon, colonel) who rode the sled himself
632 mph made him 'the fastest man on Earth' (land speed record at the time)
Face frames on screen are from an EARLIER 421 mph / 12 g run, labelled 'EARLIER RUN · 421 MPH' and in the credit
Sled animation is a simplified illustration (credit 'Curio animation · sled simplified'); speeds/timings shown match STP-1/2

not_used: Eyes 'filled with blood' payoff: only secondary sources tie it to the Dec 10 1954 run; Wikipedia describes retinal bleeding on earlier runs generally.
